title: Print Emphasis Active Highlight Mechanism
description: Port the UI's "emphasized" text-color mechanism (text-element gray default vs text-emphasized foreground, plus the active-base/active-foreground and highlight-fill primitives) into the print/tex LaTeX package. Emphasis in this design system is conveyed by swapping to the full foreground color, never italics (the print font stack has no italic face). Concretely: print/tex/semio-table.sty's \semio@table@header@cell only applies \bfseries and inherits the muted semio-chrome-text-normal body color — it needs \color{semio-chrome-foreground} so header text renders emphasized like the UI's text-emphasized on <th>. Also add reusable emphasized/active/highlight primitives in semio-core.sty mirroring the UI's text-element/text-emphasized, active-base/active-foreground, and hover-interactive-fill utility pair so future print templates can reuse them consistently.
summary: Ported the UI's foreground-color emphasis mechanism (text-element muted default vs text-emphasized foreground, plus active-base/active-foreground and highlight-fill primitives) into the print/tex LaTeX package. Added a reusable Emphasis Mechanism region in semio-core.sty (\semio@text@element, \semio@text@emphasized, \semio@active, \semio@highlighted) and redefined \emph to use the foreground-color swap instead of italics, since the print font stack has no italic face. Wired \semio@table@header@cell in semio-table.sty to use \semio@text@emphasized so table header rows render in full foreground color instead of inheriting the muted body gray. Verified by building the report template (light and dark themes) with Tectonic: TOC and register table headers now render bold in the emphasized foreground color, clearly distinct from the muted body text, in both themes.
